text:
maya: heads up — rack-22 node-gpu-07 started dropping clocks and hitting Xid/ECC messages about 09:12 UTC, observed inference tail latencies spike on prod :grimacing:
monitor-bot: ALERT rack=rack-22 node=node-gpu-07 evt=power_sag severity=warning ts=2026-03-18T09:12:34Z
kevin: can you paste the short dmesg and a quick nvidia-smi dump? also check IPMI sensors and PDU channel if you can
maya: copying snippets, short and messy but relevant
maya: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.679102] nvidia: GPU 0000:01:00.0: Xid 79
[ 12346.000000] EDAC sbridge: corrected error, socket 0
[ 12346.100000] thermal 0000:01:00.0: critical temp reached, throttling
```
maya: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,POWER -i 0
GPU Current Temp                        : 74 C
Power Readings:
    Power Draw                          : 220.50 W
    Power Limit                         : 300.00 W
GPU Utilization                         : 98 %
FB Memory Usage                         : 93 %
```
maya: ipmi sensor shows 12V rail dipping around the same time, not full dropout but jitter: "12V    | 11.2 Volts  | ok" and earlier 12.0V
maya: fans oscillating too, PWM goes 30 -> 70 -> 35 in <1m intervals, noisy logs about fan tach fluctuations
oliver: sounds like a transient PSU/PDU issue or a failing VRM on the node. If the 12V rail is dipping you can get GPU disconnects that present as Xid + ECC noise
kevin: are other nodes in rack-22 showing similar symptoms? could be a shared PDU channel or PDUs cycling under load
maya: checked three neighbors — node-gpu-05 had elevated temps but no Xid; node-gpu-08 showed a single corrected ECC earlier. pattern suggests rack-level power instability not one isolated card, but node-gpu-07 worse
monitor-bot: METRIC spike: rack22.pdu.channel3.voltage_variance = 0.9V @ 2026-03-18T09:12:30Z
kevin: safe move = drain the node, evict pods, mark unschedulable, and put it on maintenance then we can repro with power-cycling and BMC logs
maya: starting drain now, will migrate inference pods off node-gpu-07
maya: /bin/kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-gpu-07
maya: /bin/kubectl cordon node-gpu-07 && /bin/kubectl drain node-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
oliver: after drain, request on-site to swap PSU and check PDU channel. if PDU shows cycling under load we need datacenter ops to replace or move rack to different feed
kevin: log a hardware ticket with datacenter: include BMC logs, PDU channel, timestamps, and sample dmesg/nvidia logs. can you attach the BMC sdr and sel?
maya: posted SEL extract to internal storage, brief SEL entries show repeated FRU faults around 09:11-09:13, sending link in DM
sre-bot: CREATED INCIDENT INC-2026-0456 | title="rack-22 power instability affecting inference" | severity=high | owner=eng-infra
kevin: plan of record: 1) drain & isolate node-gpu-07 (done) 2) repro with PSU swap / PDU swap in staging rack if available 3) schedule replacement for node if repros fail or SEL shows persistent FRU faults 4) consider rolling minor model traffic to fallback model for 6h while we evaluate 5) add metric alert for 12V variance >0.5V across rack
maya: will keep logs and timeframe in the incident. migrating small traffic to fallback model now, monitoring latencies
oliver: FYI — if we see persistent fan PWM jitter + voltage sag, sometimes the card's onboard VRM caps age and fail under sustained high-utilization workloads. replacement recommended if swapping PSU/PDU doesn't fix it
kevin: thanks. also add a note to infra-runbook about checking PDU firmware and load-balancing GPUs across PDU circuits during heavy retraining windows
sre-bot: UPDATE INC-2026-0456 | status=investigating | notes="node drained, pods migrated, datacenter ticket opened"
maya: marking this node for hardware triage and temporary exclusion from scheduling until we confirm stability. will post final after DC ops checks :thermometer_face:
